column2: `python/final_report.py` imports the private `pr_body._read_kv` alias for pylint dedup. the plan updates `python/pr_body.py` to replace `_read_kv` with `larch_io` but does not add `python/final_report.py` or preserve a delegate. deleting the private helper breaks `final_report` kv reads at ship/closeout and can fail at import time.

`run_logs._read_kv_file` reads with strict utf-8 (no `errors="replace"`) and returns `""` on `unicodedecodeerror`. planned `larch_io.read_kv` defaults to `errors="replace"`, which would decode invalid bytes instead of failing closed to the empty default. that can change manifest/state reads on corrupt env files.

the plan only replaces `_write_text` in `design_lifecycle.py`, but issue scope and acceptance require removing duplicate env-file readers. `_read_env_value`, `_read_env_value_last`, `_read_env_values`, and related helpers have call-site-specific semantics (symlink paths return defaults; empty matched values map to default; last-wins with truthy-only updates; merged keys skip empty values). naive `read_kv`/`read_kvs` defaults would change `/design` routing and stall-report reads, and would leave duplicate parsers in place failing the one-definition acceptance criterion. `_read_env_value` specifically treats `key=` empty rhs as default, unlike generic `read_kv` returning `""`.

`_write_kv_file` is a non-atomic writer with bool `oserror` swallow that is not equivalent to `write_kvs(..., atomic=true)`. blind replacement changes write durability and error signaling for `.design-step0-route-state.env` and step 0 result env rows.

issue evidence cites `tokens.py` kv parsing and `_atomic_text` duplication, but the plan has no `tokens.py` entry. after the planned file list completes, token sidecar parsers and `_atomic_text` (with its mkstemp prefix and `newline="\n"` behavior) would remain as local duplicate definitions, failing the one-definition-per-helper acceptance criterion.

the plan removes bootstrap's `_parse_kv` but leaves `_atomic_text` and `_read_simple_kv` in `bootstrap.py` and `_atomic_text` in `admission.py` as private copies of helpers the shared module is supposed to own. post-merge grep would still find multiple atomic writers and kv readers.

`plan_review._read_kv_file` returns `{}` when `path.is_symlink()`. shared `read_kvs` has no read-side symlink handling in the plan api. replacing inline logic with bare `read_kvs` may follow symlinks and parse kv from an unexpected target.
the plan replaces `_read_kv_file` but leaves `_session_get` used by `_binary_available` and other paths. duplicate `key=value` file scan logic remains after migration.

current `plan_review_panel._parse_kv` is last-wins with no key regex. the plan prescribes `first_wins=true` and uppercase `key_pattern`, matching `implement_dispatch` instead. that can retain stale values or drop keys when stdout repeats a key, violating the no wire-format behavior change constraint.

current `implement_dispatch._parse_kv` uses `setdefault` (first occurrence wins) and accepts only `[a-z0-9_]+` keys. the plan calls plain `larch_io.parse_kv` (default last-wins, no filter). duplicate envelope keys (e.g. repeated `status=`) would resolve to the wrong value and non-envelope keys could be ingested.

`stall_recovery.read_kv` scans all lines and keeps the last matching value. planned `larch_io.read_kv` defaults to `first_match=true`, which would return the first duplicate key only. stall attempt/signature reads can pick stale values when a key appears more than once.

proposed `parse_kv` default `skip_empty_key=true` regresses most bare repoints. majority of current `_parse_kv` copies (design_publish, design_postplan, plan_review_round, ci_monitor, phantom, decompose, preflight, plan_quality, review_tally, bootstrap) store empty-key lines when present. plan lists many sites as bare `larch_io.parse_kv` without `skip_empty_key=false`. an output line `=value` is currently retained under key `""`; after bare repoint it is dropped.

`session_env._atomic_write` uses `o_creat|o_excl`, optional `o_nofollow`, explicit `fchmod`, and symlink checks on path and temp before `replace`. plan mentions `nofollow` and `mode` but not the `o_excl` create path. a weaker shared implementation could introduce symlink/temp-file races on session env writes.

shared `read_kv` defaults to `on_error_default=true`, but several planned call-site replacements do not preserve readers that currently propagate read errors. if a state/env file exists but becomes unreadable, `step_7a`, `execution_issues`, and `pr_body` paths could silently use empty/default values instead of surfacing the i/o failure.

`ci_monitor._parse_kv_output` strips all surrounding whitespace from values via `value.strip()`. plan lists ci_monitor as bare `parse_kv` while `ci_agentic_fix` is correctly specified with `strip_value=true`. `status=passed ` with trailing whitespace would fail status comparisons after repoint.

plan leaves `review_tally` read/write/append text helpers un-repointed. duplicate-helper grep would still find them alongside other review-stack copies, so the one-definition acceptance condition is not met.

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:207-210; python/plan_review_panel.py:271-277 [scope-reduction] plan adds first-wins and uppercase key filtering to a parser that is currently last-wins with no key filter. scenario: if panel or waterfall stdout emits duplicate all_output_files_path or another key, the repointed parser keeps the first value or drops non-matching keys, while current code keeps the last parsed value from every key=value line

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:228-231; python/clarify.py:316-336 [scope-reduction] plan repoints a symlink-refusing atomic output writer to plain write_text. scenario: a symlink --out-file currently raises before writing; plain write_text would follow the symlink, lose atomic replacement, and create new files with write_text umask mode instead of the current tempfile mode

`### updated: python/design_postplan.py` has no repoint steps while the module still defines duplicate `_parse_kv` and bool-return `_write_result_env`. an implementer can skip the file, leaving local copies in place and failing acceptance ("one definition per helper; duplicate copies removed") and post-refactor grep/r0801 checks.

`### updated: python/plan_review_round.py` is empty while `_parse_kv` remains a local duplicate of the centralized parser. the module can be omitted from the refactor, leaving a surviving copy and failing the dedup acceptance criterion.

plan bullets for `pr_body.py` and `execution_issues.py` document behavior preservation or edge cases but omit concrete repoint steps for path-based `_read_kv`. `final_report` may move to `larch_io`, but identical local readers can remain in both modules, violating duplicate-removal acceptance and leaving drift risk on core ship/report paths.

`### updated: python/research.py` mentions temp naming only and does not instruct replacing `_write_text_atomic`. a local atomic text writer can remain alongside repointed modules, failing duplicate-removal acceptance.

plan repoints kv helpers in `implement_dispatch.py` but not heavily used `_write_text_atomic` (~15 call sites, sibling `path.name + ".tmp"` naming). local atomic-write logic can survive and fail grep-based duplicate-removal acceptance.

`tokens.py` repoint is limited to `token_claude_source`; other hand-rolled `partition("=")` kv loops (`parse_token_record_sidecar`, `_raw_tool_from_sidecar`, lane sidecar reads) are unspecified. stragglers can remain duplicated and drift again, failing "repoint all duplicate sites" acceptance.

planned `_kv_parse` repoint to `larch_io.parse_kv` omits `skip_empty_key=true` though the current parser drops empty keys via `if key:`. default behavior would accept `=value` lines under key `""`, changing ballot/env stdout parsing semantics.
`_parse_env_lines` repoint lacks explicit `skip_empty_key=true`. current helper rejects empty-key lines with `if key:`; plain repoint would accept them and change env parsing behavior.

plan preserves `\r` stripping for file reads only; `_parse_kv` also strips `\r` from stdout-parsed values. repointing to plain `parse_kv` without equivalent kwargs would drop `.strip("\r")` on the stdout/text path.
plan repoints `_parse_kv` only; `_write_result_env` remains a third non-atomic bool-return result-env writer parallel to `design_lifecycle._write_kv_file` and `design_postplan`.
`clarify.py` covers `_write_text` / `_write_text_file` but not `_write_result_env`, a separate atomic symlink-refusing kv writer not mapped to `larch_io`.

`format_kvs` replacement does not state support for iterable key-value rows. `session_env` passes a list of tuples to `_kv_text` during finalize restore; a mapping-only `format_kvs` would raise or lose required output order.

python/session_env.py:292-297 [scope-reduction] session-env whole-file cr rejection lacks explicit preservation contract in larch_io.py new section. scenario: repointing reads through generic read_text/read_kvs without reject_cr accepts crlf env files that must fail per test_session_env.py

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:13,103-105 [scope-reduction] parse_kv is planned without an errors parameter but tokens.py call sites are planned with errors="replace". scenario: the implementation can follow the listed api and then introduce typeerror on the token_claude_source path, making the refactor fail its own parity goal

<TMPDIR>/plan.txt:81,128 [scope-reduction] write_kvs has conflicting oserror behavior between helper tests and the design_lifecycle wrapper. scenario: if write_kvs swallows oserror and returns false while the wrapper only catches exceptions, design_lifecycle._write_kv_file can report success after a failed write

the plan’s `### updated:` section for `python/file_oos.py` does not spell out how `_read_kv_file` is repointed before local helper deletion. the duplicate helper can survive, failing the one-definition-per-helper acceptance criterion and leaving `disposition_checkpoint_main` reads of `ship-pr-state.sh` / `finalize-state.sh` on a local copy. implementers may also miss parity requirements: missing-file `{}`, no symlink rejection (follow symlinks when `is_file()` is true), `errors="replace"` read semantics, and `strip_trailing_cr=true` for crlf state values.

the plan repoints `_parse_env_lines` / `_parse_env_file` but leaves `_session_get` (and `_env_get`) as hand-rolled kv readers with many call sites. after deleting other local io helpers, this module still carries duplicate kv-read logic that can drift again and fails the dedup goal.

the plan says to delete both local helpers in `python/design_postplan.py` but only specifies `_parse_kv` replacement. `_write_result_env` repoint is implied, not explicit. edge cases document the bool-swallow non-atomic pattern for `design_publish` / `design_lifecycle`, but this module’s writer step is not spelled out. an implementer may delete `_write_result_env` without a replacement, switch to atomic `write_kvs`, or use a generic repoint that misses dict-input ordering, empty-dict → empty file semantics, and bool-return `oserror` swallow used at the call site (e.g. line 117).

the session-env `atomic_write` repoint does not pin the sibling `with_suffix` + `o_excl` temp contract. current code uses `path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")`, pre-unlink, `o_creat|o_excl` (+ `o_nofollow`), and `fchmod`; a generic mkstemp-style `atomic_write` changes temp placement and race semantics covered by `test_session_env.py`.

`_parse_env_lines` replacement is left unresolved ("only if") despite `allowed_keys` / `key_pattern` support. an implementer may leave a duplicate parser or repoint without `routing_keys` / `_key_re`, changing bootstrap routing env filtering.

`_write_text` duplicate is not repointed; the "preserve parent creation" bullet targets the wrong helper. preflight keeps a local mkdir+write helper, and the misplaced bullet adds implementer confusion.

dict-based `read_kv`/`read_kvs` cannot preserve last-nonempty env semantics. the plan routes `_read_env_value_last` and `_read_env_values` through `larch_io.read_kv`/`read_kvs`, but current code ignores empty duplicate values instead of letting them overwrite prior nonempty values. a file with `foo=ok` followed by `foo=` would currently return `ok`, while the planned dict or last-match read can return default or empty.

parsing to a string dict before float conversion changes duplicate-key behavior. current `_parse_kv` keeps the last parseable float and ignores later non-float values. the plan parses with `larch_io.parse_kv` first, so `key=1.0` followed by `key=bad` leaves only bad to convert and drops `key` entirely.

plan marks `stall_recovery.read_kv` as best-effort even though current read errors propagate. current `read_kv` only defaults for non-files. `oserror` from an existing file read is not caught. the planned `on_error_default=true` would hide read failures and change the public `stall_recovery.read_kv` contract.

plan deletes `bootstrap._atomic_text` but misses the test that monkeypatches it. `python/test_bootstrap.py` still reads and monkeypatches `bootstrap._atomic_text`. if the helper is removed per plan, this test fails before exercising the routing-write failure path.

the plan lists `python/plan_review_round.py` but its `### updated:` section is empty while the module still defines and uses local `_parse_kv` (lines 625, 724, 781, 820). after a literal plan follow, a fifth duplicate last-wins `key=value` parser survives, failing acceptance ("one definition per helper; duplicate copies removed") and the post-refactor duplicate-helper grep check.

the `_env_get` repoint in `review_and_fix.py` is specified with `larch_io.read_kv(..., first_match=true)`, but current `_parse_env_lines` is last-wins. an env file with duplicate keys (e.g. two `scout_coder_status=` lines) would return the first value instead of the last; `_env_get` drives scout status routing.

the `_read_kv_raw` repoint omits `skip_comments=true` while the local loop skips `line.startswith("#")`. env files with commented kv lines like `# foo=bar` would parse to key `# foo` under plain `larch_io.parse_kv`, changing session-env reads covered by `test_session_env.py`.

`strip_trailing_cr` homogenizes divergent cr stripping semantics across call sites. today: `bootstrap._parse_kv` uses `value.rstrip("\r")`, `bootstrap._read_simple_kv` uses `removesuffix("\r")`, while `pr_body`, `execution_issues`, `stall_recovery`, `file_oos`, and `oos_filer` use `value.strip("\r")`. a single trailing-only knob can change rhs bytes on repoint.

`test_admission.py` monkeypatch target is omitted from the test-update plan. the plan deletes `admission._atomic_text` but only lists `test_bootstrap.py` / `test_session_env.py` for atomic-write monkeypatch migration. `test_admission.py` patches `admission._atomic_text` for caller-env write-failure simulation and will fail or stop exercising the path.

issue-cited `_read_simple_env` duplicate near `design_lifecycle.py:2978` is not covered. the plan repoints `_read_env_value*` but is silent on `_read_simple_env`, which still hand-rolls allowlisted `key=value` parsing used in dirty-tree / step5c paths.

`larch_io.atomic_write(..., exclusive=true)` must unlink an existing fixed sibling temp (e.g. `.tmp`) before `os.open(..., o_creat|o_excl)`. `session_env._atomic_write` already does this; without parity, a stale `.tmp` from a prior crash or interrupted write raises `fileexistserror` and breaks session-env / launcher resume and retry paths covered by `test_session_env.py`.

`plan_review._write_atomic` repoint omits `create_parent=false`. the current helper never calls `mkdir`; `larch_io.atomic_write` defaults `create_parent=true`, so a missing parent would silently succeed instead of failing, changing wire/env sidecar behavior on edge paths.

`progress_report._read_simple_env` is a third copy of simple kv-from-file parsing but is neither repointed nor listed as a deliberate grep exception. acceptance requires one definition per helper and a duplicate-helper grep with only documented exceptions; this helper will fail that gate.

`python/agents.py` io duplicates left as `may_update` but omitted from acceptance grep exceptions. acceptance requires duplicate helper copies removed and testing strategy ends with a duplicate-helper grep against expected exceptions; `progress_report` and `dirty_tree` are named deferrals but `agents.py` `_read_text`/`_write`/`_append`/`_review_atomic_write_text` are not, so the run can ship with four remaining text-io clones while the stated acceptance criterion reads unmet or an operator over-expands scope into `agents.py` mid-refactor.

plan leaves a simple local kv parser (`_parse_text_kv`) outside `larch_io`. the acceptance contract requires duplicate kv helpers to be removed, but `_parse_text_kv` would remain as another `key=value` parser after the proposed `session_env` repoints.

plan does not preserve `oserror` fallback on best-effort design env readers. current readers return the default or `{}` when an existing env sidecar cannot be read; a direct `read_text` repoint can raise and abort design recovery or postplan paths.
